documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT - PREVENTIVE

24 y/o man establishing care. Grew up in the area, finished college, now a marketing associate at a firm in town. Last physical was a few years ago through his old practice; records release signed today.

He feels well. No complaints. Plays pickup basketball once a week, runs a couple of miles on weekends.

PMH: none.
PSH: wisdom teeth out at 18.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father - hypertension, diagnosed in his mid-40s. Maternal grandmother - type 2 diabetes. No early heart disease or cancers he knows of.
SHx: single, lives alone in an apartment. Never smoked, no vaping. Drinks socially, 3-4 drinks a week, rarely more than two at a time. No drug use. Sexually active; not in a steady relationship; condoms "most of the time."

ROS negative in full.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted.
HEENT normal, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid not enlarged. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without rash. Extremities warm, no edema. Neuro grossly intact. Genital exam deferred, declined, no complaints.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 3.

A/P: healthy young man.
- Routine labs: CBC, CMP, lipid panel.
- One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening per guidelines - agreeable.
- Vaccines: last Tdap was at 11 per his memory, so Tdap today. Flu shot today. Never had HPV vaccine; eligible through 26 - dose 1 of 3 today, then 2 and 6 months.
- Safer sex: discussed condoms and periodic STI testing; he can message us any time.
- Return yearly; message for anything sooner.

documents.title: Injection and reaction
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
16:02 Pt here for Bicillin L-A per order. Denied prior reactions to any antibiotic. Pre-injection VS as charted.
16:05 Bicillin L-A 2.4 million units (2 x 1.2 MU syringes) deep IM, R and L ventrogluteal. Pt seated for observation.
16:14 Pt reports itching and "my throat feels tight." Raised wheals over chest, neck and arms. Audible wheeze. Dr notified, came immediately.
16:16 BP 86/52, HR 118, SpO2 93% RA. Pt placed supine, legs up.
16:17 Epinephrine 1 mg/mL, 0.3 mg IM R anterolateral thigh per verbal order. 911 called by front desk. O2 by nasal cannula 2 L.
16:27 BP 108/68, HR 104, SpO2 97%. Wheeze softer, speaking full sentences. Hives persist but fading.
16:34 EMS arrived; report given, copy of MAR sent. Transported to the ED in stable condition.

documents.title: Addendum - anaphylaxis after benzathine penicillin
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Called to the injection room ~10 min after Bicillin L-A for urticaria, throat tightness and wheeze with hypotension (86/52) and tachycardia. Anaphylaxis. IM epinephrine 0.3 mg given at 16:17 with quick improvement in BP and breathing; EMS transported him to the ED for observation (biphasic risk).
- PENICILLIN ALLERGY - ANAPHYLAXIS entered in the chart, high criticality.
- Syphilis treatment: he received the full 2.4 MU dose before the reaction, so treatment is complete. Serologic follow-up at 6 and 12 months as planned.
- Will call him tomorrow.

documents.title: Emergency department record - 2/11/2019
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Visit date: 02/11/2019, arrival 16:51 by ambulance. Received by fax 02/12/2019.

HPI: 25M sent from his PCP office after anaphylaxis to IM benzathine penicillin given at ~16:05 for syphilis. Received IM epinephrine 0.3 mg at the office ~16:17. On arrival reports mild itch, no throat tightness, breathing comfortably.
Allergies: penicillin (anaphylaxis - today).
Exam: alert, no distress. Scattered fading urticaria on trunk. No stridor, no lip or tongue swelling. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Heart regular. Injection sites unremarkable.
ED course: diphenhydramine 50 mg IV, famotidine 20 mg IV, methylprednisolone 125 mg IV. Observed 6 hours on monitor without recurrence. Repeat vitals normal.
Impression: Anaphylaxis to penicillin, resolved.
Disposition: discharged home 23:10. Avoid all penicillins; tell every provider and pharmacy. Follow up with PCP.

documents.title: Post-ED check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Called pt the morning after. Home from the ED around 11:30 last night. Feels "wiped out" but no hives, swelling or trouble breathing. Went back to work today. Confirmed he knows to avoid penicillin and amoxicillin family and to list it as an anaphylaxis allergy everywhere. Urine GC/CT from yesterday negative - told him.
Partner notification: he has reached out to the one partner by message. Gave him the state partner services number as well. Syphilis case report faxed to DPH.
Dr aware.

documents.author: urology

OUTSIDE UROLOGY GROUP - OFFICE NOTE
Date of visit: 08/02/2019. Faxed to PCP 08/06/2019.

Reason: self-referred for same-day appointment.
HPI: 25-year-old man with three days of dysuria and a yellow discharge from the penis. Unprotected intercourse with a new partner about two weeks ago. Prior history of a penile ulcer earlier this year, treated by his PCP.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
PMH: syphilis, primary, treated 2019. PSH: wisdom teeth.
SHx: nonsmoker, social alcohol, works in marketing.

Exam: VS within normal limits. Purulent discharge expressed at the meatus. No skin rash. No inguinal lymphadenopathy. No joint swelling or tenderness. Testes and epididymides normal to palpation.

Studies: urine NAAT positive for N. gonorrhoeae, negative for C. trachomatis (resulted 8/3). UA: no evidence of urinary tract infection.

Impression: gonococcal urethritis.
Plan: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM given in the office today, observed 30 minutes without incident. Abstain for 7 days after treatment and until partner(s) treated. Partner to be evaluated and treated. Retest in 3 months. Follow up with PCP for ongoing STI screening.

documents.title: Office Visit - follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here to follow up. Saw an outside urologist on 8/2 for discharge and burning (letter in chart): GC positive, CT negative, given ceftriaxone 500 IM. He told them "no allergies" - he says he wasn't thinking of the shot here as an allergy. He had no reaction at all to the ceftriaxone, observed 30 min. Symptoms gone within two days. Partner was told and got treated.

Reviewed again: penicillin = anaphylaxis, must always be listed. He has put a note in his phone.

Exam: well. Vitals as charted. No meatal discharge. Prior chancre site healed with no scar.

A/P:
1. Primary syphilis, treated 2/2019 - 6-month RPR today; diagnosis closed on the list as treated, titer follow-up continues.
2. Gonococcal urethritis - treated by urology. Tolerated a cephalosporin despite penicillin anaphylaxis; noted for the future. Retest urine in ~3 months.
3. HIV Ag/Ab repeat today.
4. Condoms every time with new partners - he agrees, says the summer has been "a lot."

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: RPR now 1:8, down from 1:32 in February - a fourfold drop, which is the response we want. HIV nonreactive. Portal message sent. Next RPR at 12 months (February).

documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN NOTE
Date of service: 02/11/2020. Copy to PCP, received 02/13/2020.

CC: L testicle pain.
HPI: 26M with prior primary syphilis (2019) and gonococcal urethritis (2019) presents at 1:30 am with two days of left testicular pain, steadily worse, now severe. Felt feverish at home. Notes a thin clear discharge from the penis. No dysuria, no flank or back pain, no trauma. Sexually active with multiple partners; uses condoms inconsistently.
Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: T 38.1 at triage, other VS normal. Uncomfortable. Left testis markedly tender and swollen; overlying scrotal skin erythematous, no lesions, no crepitus. Cremasteric reflex present. Right testis normal. No CVA tenderness. Abdomen soft.
Labs/imaging: UA 10-20 WBC/hpf. Urine NAAT positive for chlamydia, negative for gonorrhea. Scrotal US: left epididymitis, normal testicular flow, no torsion, no abscess.
Dx: Acute left epididymitis, chlamydial.
Treatment: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM in ED. Rx doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 10 days. Ibuprofen and scrotal support for pain. Partners within 60 days need treatment. Return for worsening pain, high fever, vomiting.
Dispo: home 06:10. PCP follow-up this week.

documents.author: RN
documents.body:
ED record received 2/13: L epididymitis, chlamydia +, ceftriaxone in ED and doxycycline x 10 days. Note: ED list says NKDA - pt has PENICILLIN ANAPHYLAXIS (2/2019). Cephalosporin again tolerated per pt, no rash.
Called pt: pain "maybe half of what it was," no fever since Tuesday, taking doxy with food. Booked with PCP Wed 2/19. Chlamydia case report to DPH done.

ED 2/11 for L epididymitis, chlamydia NAAT positive, US without torsion. Got ceftriaxone there and is on doxycycline 100 BID, day 8 today. Pain and swelling much better, ache only at the end of the day. No fever, no discharge now. No GI upset with the doxy.

Sexual history: since last summer several partners, condoms not consistent. Three STIs in a year. We talked frankly - he says he knows, and he wants to do better about condoms.
Allergies: penicillin - anaphylaxis (ED list again said NKDA; reminded him to tell them).

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Left epididymis mildly thickened and barely tender; testis normal. Right side normal. No discharge.

A/P:
1. Left epididymitis, chlamydial - improving, finish the 10-day course. Retest urine in 3 months.
2. Syphilis, treated 2/2019 - 12-month RPR today.
3. HIV Ag/Ab today.
4. High-risk sexual behavior - added to the problem list. Condoms, regular screening every visit, and come in with any new symptom.

documents.title: Emergency department and observation record - 2/4-2/5/2022
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT / OBSERVATION UNIT
Dates: 02/04/2022 19:20 - 02/05/2022 12:30. Records to PCP 02/07/2022.

HPI: 28-year-old man, history of primary syphilis, gonococcal urethritis and epididymitis, here with a week of fevers, headache and a spreading rash over his chest, back, arms and legs. Recent condomless sex with multiple partners. No medications. Allergies: NKDA.
Exam: T 38.7, HR 102, BP 124/72, SpO2 98%. Ill-appearing but alert and oriented. Diffuse blanching maculopapular eruption on trunk and extremities; palms and soles spared. Nuchal rigidity present. No focal deficits. No oral ulcers noted.
Labs: WBC 9.0, Hgb 14, Plt 250. Glucose 90.
LP (21:40): opening pressure not recorded. CSF WBC 50 with lymphocytic predominance, protein 50, glucose 60 (serum 90). Gram stain no organisms. Culture no growth at 48 h.
RPR nonreactive. Monospot negative. HIV-1/2 Ag/Ab REACTIVE (resulted 2/5 09:15). HIV-1 RNA and CD4 sent.
Course: CSF pattern lymphocytic with normal glucose; empiric antibiotics not started. Acetaminophen and fluids. Observed overnight; headache improved, fever down to 37.6 by morning. ID consulted by phone - favors acute retroviral syndrome with lymphocytic meningitis; arranged rapid-start visit in ID clinic 2/9.
Impression: Acute HIV infection (acute retroviral syndrome) with aseptic/lymphocytic meningitis.
Disposition: home 2/5 12:30. Counselled on transmission risk; abstain until seen by ID. Return for confusion, worsening headache, vomiting. PCP follow-up after ID.

documents.title: PCP call after ED record
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ED record received this morning. Acute HIV with lymphocytic meningitis; Ag/Ab reactive. ED lab released the rest today: HIV-1 RNA 2,400,000 copies/mL, CD4 380. CSF culture no growth.
Called Miles. Headache nearly gone, fever off since Saturday, rash fading. He is shaken but has a friend with him this week. Talked through what this means now: daily treatment, normal life expectancy, undetectable = untransmittable once suppressed. ID visit Wed 2/9 is confirmed; I sent our referral and records so they have the penicillin anaphylaxis and his syphilis history. See me after.
Partner services: DPH will reach out; he consented.

OUTSIDE INFECTIOUS DISEASE CLINIC - NEW PATIENT CONSULTATION
Date of visit: 02/09/2022. Copy to PCP.

Referred by PCP and the ED for newly diagnosed HIV-1 in the setting of acute retroviral syndrome (fever, rash, lymphocytic meningitis, 2/4). Ag/Ab reactive, HIV-1 RNA 2,400,000 copies/mL, CD4 380.
Today: headache resolved, no fever for 3 days, faint residual rash on the back. No thrush, no weight loss.
History: syphilis 2019 (treated, RPR now nonreactive), gonorrhea 2019, chlamydial epididymitis 2020.
Allergies: penicillin - anaphylaxis 2019. Meds: none.

Exam: well. Vitals normal. Faint macular rash posterior trunk. No adenopathy of note. Neuro normal.

Assessment: acute HIV-1 infection.
Plan:
- Rapid ART start today: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 50/200/25 mg, one tablet daily. First dose taken in clinic. Specialty pharmacy enrollment and copay card done.
- Baseline genotype (sent at ED draw): no resistance mutations detected.
- Hepatitis B: sAg negative, sAb positive - immune. Hepatitis C Ab negative. Renal function and UA normal.
- Repeat viral load and CD4 in 4-6 weeks.
- Counselled on adherence, U=U, condoms for other STIs.
- We will manage ART and HIV labs; PCP continues primary care, vaccines and STI screening.

documents.author: PCP

Follow-up after the ED stay 2/4-2/5 (acute HIV, lymphocytic meningitis) and ID intake 2/9.
Feels "basically back to normal." No fever since 2/5, headache resolved, rash gone. Started bictegravir/FTC/TAF 2/9, one pill every morning with his coffee, no missed doses, no side effects. Lost a couple of pounds while sick.
Mood: anxious at first, better now that he has a plan. Sleeping. Told two close friends; feels supported. PHQ-9 4.
Allergies: penicillin - anaphylaxis. Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1 tab daily (ID).

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Skin clear. No meningismus. No lymphadenopathy. Heart and lungs normal.

A/P:
1. Acute HIV infection - on ART per ID; their letter reviewed. ID owns HIV labs.
2. Prevention now that he has HIV: pneumococcal (PCV20) and two-dose MenACWY - will give at his fall physical once he is settled on ART, plus flu and COVID updates.
3. STI screening continues here, at least yearly.
4. Mood - normal adjustment, PHQ-9 low. Open door; can message any time.

documents.title: Office Visit - penile ulcer
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Painless sore on the penile shaft first noticed about 3 weeks ago, same size since. No discharge from it or from the urethra. No fever, rash, headache, vision or hearing change. Over the last ~6 months has had condomless sex with several partners. Last RPR nonreactive in October.
History: syphilis 2019 (treated; RPR nonreactive by 2021), gonorrhea 2019, chlamydial epididymitis 2020, HIV since 2022 - suppressed on ART, last ID visit 8/2025.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide 1 tab daily.
Allergies: PENICILLIN - anaphylaxis in this office 2/2019 (needed epinephrine and the ED). Has tolerated ceftriaxone twice since.

O: Afebrile, vitals as charted.
GU: solitary firm, indurated ulcer on the shaft, painless to touch, clean base. Bilateral inguinal nodes enlarged, rubbery, mobile, non-tender, not fluctuant. No urethral discharge. Testes normal.
Skin: no rash on trunk, palms or soles. Mouth clear. Neuro: normal.

A: Indurated painless ulcer with rubbery inguinal adenopathy in a man with prior syphilis and new exposures - primary syphilis, reinfection, most likely.

P:
- RPR with titer today (prior titer nonreactive, so any reactive titer means new infection), urine GC/CT. Treponemal test not useful - positive since 2019.
- Treatment: penicillin is out given anaphylaxis. For primary syphilis, doxycycline 100 mg twice daily x 14 days is the accepted alternative, with close titer follow-up; desensitization is the other route and we can revisit if the titer doesn't fall. Will start once the RPR is back this afternoon.
- No sex until the sore is healed and treatment done; partners in the last 3 months need testing/treatment.
- Letter to ID.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth twice daily for 14 days with a full glass of water; stay upright 30 minutes

Addendum 15:20: GC/CT not detected; pt informed via portal.

documents.title: Office Visit - syphilis follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Finished the 14 days of doxycycline on 2/9, every dose, no side effects. The sore shrank within a week and is gone. Groin lumps smaller. No rash, headache or vision change. Has not been sexually active since the visit.
Meds: bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide daily (ID). Allergies: penicillin - anaphylaxis.

Exam: vitals as charted. Penile shaft: ulcer healed, faint pink macule at the site. Inguinal nodes now small, soft, non-tender. Skin clear including palms and soles. Neuro normal.

A/P:
1. Primary syphilis (reinfection), treated with doxycycline 14 days - clinical response good. RPR at 3 and 6 months (orders in, standing), then 9 and 12. Expect a fourfold drop by 6-12 months; if it doesn't come, revisit penicillin desensitization with ID.
2. HIV - cleaned up the problem list: "acute HIV infection" from 2022 updated to HIV disease; on ART, suppressed per ID. ID aware of this episode.
3. Prevention: condoms; screening every 3 months while partners change. He'll book a visit for the fall.
